info.title: strictbudget API
info.description:
Zero-based budgeting API. Money amounts are integer strings in the currency's minor units.

**Authentication:** create a personal API key in the web app (Account settings → API Keys) and send it as `Authorization: Bearer ec_…`. Choose it under *Authentication* to try requests here.

apiKeyAuth.description: A personal API key (`ec_…`), created in the web app under Account → API keys and sent as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (or an `x-api-key` header). A key acts as its owner within its scope: read-only or read & write, on every budget or chosen ones. It can't reach account or security routes, create, delete or import budgets, or manage sharing; those take a signed-in session. Each key may make 500 requests an hour.

q.description: Search: comma-separated terms that must all match, each free text (payee, category, memo or account name, or an exact amount) or one of `Payee:`, `Category:` (`Category: Split` for splits), `Memo:`, `Account:`, `Flag:` (a color, its name or None), `Is:` (Uncleared, Cleared, Reconciled, Unreconciled, Cleared or Reconciled, Approved, Unapproved, Needs Category, Unapproved or Needs Category), `Outflow:`/`Inflow:` (`25`, `>=25`, `<=25`), `On:`/`Before:`/`After:` (a date in the budget's format, or part of one completed from today: `5` is May 1st in MM/DD/YYYY; before and after include the day), `Income:` (a month name, full or three letters, with an optional year, e.g. `Income: October 2026`: what's in Ready to Assign that month, including Starting Balances of budget accounts; no year means this year). post.description: Locks every cleared transaction dated up to `date` (they become reconciled, for good) and records when. If `balance` differs from the cleared balance, a Reconciliation Balance Adjustment for the difference comes first, dated `date` (budget accounts take it from Ready to Assign; tracking accounts have no category). A loan (Update Balance) is compared with its working balance, every transaction up to `date` is reconciled, and each month's interest and escrow are fixed at what's applied. A loan's `loanTerms` (Update Balance's interest rate / escrow check) change its terms from `date`'s month first; the adjustment then makes up the difference to the balance with this month re-estimated on the new terms, while the months are fixed at what they had.

post.summary: Apply one action to every selected transaction it applies to
post.description: Follows the action bar: rows an action doesn't apply to are skipped, and `updated` counts the rest. `cleared` skips reconciled rows. `categorize` skips transfers within the budget and tracking-account rows; it un-splits splits, except splits with a transfer line, which stay split with every other line given the category. `memo` replaces the memo (a split's own, not its lines'; on the selected side of a transfer only, as Edit Memo does). `move` moves rows to another account like a single edit (a transfer keeps its other side, which then points at the new account) and skips rows already there, transfers into their own other account and splits with a transfer line to it. `delete` deletes transfers' other sides too and skips the other sides of splits' transfer lines (they go with the split). `approve` approves the unapproved rows (and their transfers' other sides); `reject` deletes the unapproved rows (as `delete` does) and skips the rest; `cleared` and `categorize` approve the rows they change. `duplicate` copies each row with the same date and fields, cleared state kept (reconciled becomes cleared), approved, a transfer with a new other side; a split's transfer side copies its whole split, and a transfer selected from both sides is copied once. Rows in (or transferring to) closed accounts are skipped. All of it happens in one database transaction.

patch.summary: Edit a transaction, move it to another account, or toggle cleared
patch.description: On-budget accounts: a null category means Uncategorized; credit-card payment categories can't be used. Tracking accounts never have a category. The payee is matched by name (ignoring case) and created if new; null leaves it empty. `transferAccountId` (instead of `payeeName`) makes it a transfer: a matching transaction with the opposite amount is kept in that account. Only a transfer from a budget account to a tracking account has a category (on the budget side), as money leaves the budget. New transfers need both accounts open. Between accounts in different currencies each side has its own amount (`transferAmount`, in the other account's currency) and the two always have opposite base amounts: a side in the budget's currency sets it, otherwise the entered side at its rate; the other side's `fxRate` is the rate its amounts imply. On a transfer, date, amount and memo changes apply to both sides; cleared, flag and category are per side. Setting `payeeName` turns a transfer back into a normal transaction and deletes the other side. A reconciled other side follows and stays reconciled. A reconciled transaction can be edited but stays reconciled, so `cleared` can't be set on it. Moving it to an account that can't use its category resets the category. `subtransactions` (two or more lines, adding up to the amount) splits it across categories; its own `categoryId` is then null. Lines follow the same category and transfer rules. Only budget accounts have splits, and a transfer can't be split (its lines can be transfers). Sending `subtransactions` replaces a split's lines (matched by `id`); changing a split's amount needs new lines too. Giving a split a `categoryId` (or making it a transfer) un-splits it. A split's transfer side only takes memo, cleared, flag and category; its memo is the split line's too.

get.description: Columns: Account, Flag, Date, Payee, Category Group/Category, Category Group, Category, Memo, Outflow, Inflow, Cleared, plus Currency, FX Rate, Base Outflow and Base Inflow when the budget has an account in another currency. A split is one row per line, memo "Split (i/n) …". Starts with a UTF-8 byte-order mark. Comma-separated, or tab-separated when the budget's number format uses a comma as its decimal mark. Text cells are quoted; amounts are bare, in the budget's number format with no group separator. Lines end with CRLF. Streamed.
